main_text.p: οἰκεῖν. deinde scribe, ἐὰν ἔτι μέλλῃς : non διότι μέλλει. διότι μέλλει πωλεῖν αὐτῷ.) Ipsissimum hoc ἀλαζο-νείας genus notatum apud Athenæum lib. x i i i. Θαΐς, inquit, ἐρᾷ τι: ὃς αὐτῆς ἀλαζὼν [?] ἀφ' [illegible, ~6 letters] πολλῶν πόλεια χρημάτων, [?] ἐ λέ[?]γει [?] ταῦτα συλλογάς [?], ἀλλὰ ἢ καθ' ἑαυτὸν [?] ἐφ' ἑαυτοῦ τὸ εἶναι. Quidam, ait, qui Thaidem amabat, cum à multis pocula commodata accepisset, diceretque velle se ea conflare, Perdes, inquit illa, uninscuiusque quod suum est.

Atque hîc scribendi finem faciemus: & simul cum vertente anno, animi nostri metem alió con-uertemus. Commodùm enim cum hæc scriberem dies agebatur anni huius xc1. nouissimus. quæ me res admonebat ut duplicis voti reas DEo OPT. MAX. grates agerem gratissimas: & quod annum hunc uiuenti valentique dede it exigere: & quòd hunc commentariolum in hacce rutuba ab-soluere. qua opera si doctorum virorum studia promerui, iuniorum etiam promoui, bene ha-bet: feci quod volui: sin autem, ὁ μὴ ἡδύς [?] ἔσαι, feci quod potui.

page.notes: The Greek in the first paragraph, especially the lines beginning "Θαΐς" and "ἀλαζὼν", is small and partly blurred. Readings marked [?] are doubtful, and the stretch after "ἀφ'" is illegible. The final Greek phrase is also doubtful. The Latin is clear. The first paragraph continues from the previous page. The printed text reads "ut" as "vt" and was normalised to "ut" under the u/v rule. "Quidam" passage is set in italic. No marginal notes, catchword or signature are visible.
